module.sensitive_files.checks: Looks for files that should never be served: source repository (.git, .svn), secrets (.env and variants), configuration backups, SQL dumps, .htaccess, phpinfo, validating their content and discarding the server's catch-all "not found" page.
module.sensitive_files.fix:
Treat every readable secret as compromised: immediately change the passwords, API keys, tokens and secrets contained in the exposed file (`.env`, `wp-config.php.bak`, SQL dump, `.git` repository) at each service concerned (database, mail, cloud, payment), even before removing the file.
Remove the file from the web server: delete backups, `phpinfo.php`, `info.php` and `.DS_Store`, or move them outside the web root. For a repository (`.git`, `.svn`), do not deploy the working folder: deploy a clean export (`git archive`) or the build output.
If a `.git` repository was readable, assume all the code and its history were copied: look for secrets in the history and rotate them, even if they are gone from the current version.
Block access to hidden files, repositories and backups in the configuration so that a future mistake is not exposed: use the snippet for nginx, Apache or IIS.
Review the server access logs and those of the services concerned since the likely date of exposure to spot suspicious use (unknown logins, database exports). If personal data may have been accessed, assess your notification obligation (GDPR: 72 hours).
Keep configuration and secrets outside the web root (environment variables, secrets manager); remove `phpinfo` from production; if a `.htaccess` is served as-is, fix the server, which should never send it.
Check each reported path with `curl -sI https://example.com/.env` (expected response: `403` or `404`), then run the scan again.
module.sensitive_files.fix_snippet:
# nginx
location ~ /\.(?!well-known) {
    deny all;
}
location ~* \.(bak|old|orig|sql|swp|env)$ {
    deny all;
}

# Apache
<FilesMatch "^\.|\.(bak|old|orig|sql|swp)$">
    Require all denied
</FilesMatch>
<DirectoryMatch "/\.(git|svn)(/|$)">
    Require all denied
</DirectoryMatch>

# IIS
<system.webServer>
  <security>
    <requestFiltering>
      <hiddenSegments>
        <add segment=".git" />
        <add segment=".svn" />
      </hiddenSegments>
      <fileExtensions>
        <add fileExtension=".env" allowed="false" />
        <add fileExtension=".bak" allowed="false" />
        <add fileExtension=".sql" allowed="false" />
      </fileExtensions>
    </requestFiltering>
  </security>
</system.webServer>
module.sensitive_files.title: Exposed sensitive files
module.sensitive_files.why: An accessible .env file, configuration backup or .git repository leaks passwords, keys and source code: it is one of the most common causes of compromise.
sensitive_files.score_critical: Critical sensitive file exposed (secret or source code)
